questions.q: What Syslog facilities does Mara prioritize when setting up Linux ingestion?
options: Only kernel messages
auth, authpriv, daemon, and cron -- authentication and scheduled-task activity first
Only print-spooler logs
None -- Linux can't send Syslog to Sentinel
questions.explain: Authentication and scheduled-task activity are the most likely places something actionable shows up first.

questions.q: How does the perimeter firewall's log data reach Sentinel's CommonSecurityLog table?
options: Directly from the firewall with no intermediate step
Exported as CEF to a Linux box running the AMA, which relays the CEF stream into CommonSecurityLog
By email attachment
It cannot reach Sentinel at all
questions.explain: CEF forwarding requires the firewall's export config, the forwarder's listener, and the AMA's CEF collection rule to all agree.

questions.q: What did Network Administrator Derek Shaw intend to scope the TEMP-MERIDIAN-RDP rule to, and what did he actually save?
options: Intended 203.0.113.16/28 (Meridian's real range); actually saved 203.0.0.0/16, carried over unchanged from an old template
Intended 203.0.0.0/16; actually saved 203.0.113.16/28
He intended and saved the exact same scope -- there is no mistake
He intended to block the connection entirely
questions.explain: Derek updated the source address from an old field-office template but the template's /16 mask came along unchanged, instead of being narrowed to Meridian's real /28.

questions.q: Why did nobody notice the mistake during the vendor session?
options: The firewall logged an explicit error about the oversized range
Meridian's real IP falls inside the broad /16 range too, so the one connection anyone was watching worked exactly as expected
Derek double-checked the CIDR mask and confirmed it was correct
The session failed, which is how it was caught
questions.explain: Because Meridian's actual address is inside both the intended /28 and the accidental /16, the only connection anyone observed worked perfectly, with no visible symptom.

questions.q: What is the real difference in size between a /28 and a /16 address range?
options: They cover the same number of addresses
A /28 covers 16 addresses; a /16 covers 65,536 -- a difference of four orders of magnitude
A /28 is larger than a /16
The difference is only cosmetic and has no security implication
questions.explain: /28 = 16 addresses, /16 = 65,536 addresses -- the rule as saved trusts far more of the internet than Meridian's actual gateway range.
